name: BELOTE
description: Belote is the national card game of France, a 32-card partnership trick-taking game descended from the Jass family. It is renowned for its unique trump ranking system where the Jack ('J' or 'Valet') and the 9 ('Neuf') become the two most powerful cards, dwarfing the Ace. Players bid to establish a trump suit, declare melds ('Tierce', 'Quarte'), and strive to reach 501 or 1000 points. The term 'Belote' specifically refers to the King and Queen of Trumps held together, a declaration that can swing the game.

content.text: Belote is the national card game of France, a 32-card partnership trick-taking game descended from the Jass family. It is renowned for its unique trump ranking system where the Jack ('J' or 'Valet') and the 9 ('Neuf') become the two most powerful cards, dwarfing the Ace. Players bid to establish a trump suit, declare melds ('Tierce', 'Quarte'), and strive to reach 501 or 1000 points. The term 'Belote' specifically refers to the King and Queen of Trumps held together, a declaration that can swing the game.
Believed to be derived from the Dutch game 'Klaverjas', brought to France by diamond merchants or Jewish communities in the early 20th century.
4 players in fixed partnerships (North-South vs East-West).
Standard 32-card French pack (Piquet deck), score pad.

Deal 5 cards to each player (3-2). One card is turned face up (The Proposal). Players bid to take it as trump. If all pass, a second round of bidding allows naming any other suit. Remaining cards are dealt (3 each) for a total of 8.

items.text: Belote Coinchée: All cards are dealt at once. Players bid for points (e.g., '100 Spades') instead of simple acceptance. Opponents can 'Coinche' (Double).
Belote Découverte: Open-hand variant for 2 players. 6 cards in hand, 6 face-up on table.
